children: The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission launched an inquiry shortly after the debut of President Donald Trump’s official meme coin, Official Trump (TRUMP), but halted it over concerns it would struggle to secure approval to issue subpoenas, the New York Times reported.

According to the Nov. 20 report, CFTC enforcement staff began looking into large profits generated during TRUMP’s initial trading shortly after the token launched. TRUMP drew intense market attention as its price surged in the first 48 hours of trading. Media reports then raised questions about the trading after some early buyers reaped huge gains in a short period.

CFTC officials opened the inquiry in response to those reports, but did not proceed with follow-up steps amid concern that the commission might not approve the subpoena authority needed for the investigation.

The report did not say whether an actual subpoena request was rejected or whether investigators found specific signs of wrongdoing. Halting the inquiry also does not mean the trading was deemed lawful.

A third gala dinner for TRUMP token holders is scheduled for Sunday. As trading in the Trump-linked meme coin and events for holders continue, attention is also focused on how regulators respond to questions surrounding the token’s early trading.

title: US CFTC Probed Trump Meme Coin Fraud Allegations, Then Halted Inquiry Over Subpoena Concerns
